answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed identity: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. A shared reputation ledger acts like a mirror, reflecting each agent's past behaviour for all to see, while a signed audit trail — the quill that records every deal — makes sock-puppets easy to spot. The zenith of this design is that honest work earns trust, and sybils simply cannot afford to fake it at scale.
